name: payments-stripe
title: Payments with Stripe
description: Stripe Checkout, subscriptions and the customer portal without the SDK: allowlisted prices, redirect allowlist, one customer per user, signed webhooks processed exactly once, plan checks for routes (meta: { plan }, 'plan-pro' policies) and billing.* events. Zero dependencies.
docs:
1. List what you sell in calm.config.js: blocks: { 'payments-stripe': { prices: { price_123: 'pro', price_456: { plan: 'lifetime', mode: 'payment' } } } }. Set STRIPE_SECRET_KEY and STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET in .env.
2. Point a Stripe webhook at APP_URL/api/billing/webhook (locally: stripe listen --forward-to localhost:5001/api/billing/webhook).
3. POST /api/billing/checkout { price } -> { id, url }: redirect the browser to url. POST /api/billing/portal -> { url }. GET /api/billing -> { plan, status, currentPeriodEnd, cancelAtPeriodEnd, ... }. GET /api/billing/prices lists what is on sale.
Gate routes with meta: { plan: 'pro' } (402 PLAN_REQUIRED) or policy: 'plan-pro'. React with calm.on('billing.subscription_updated' | 'billing.payment_failed' | ...).
agents:
Read app/blocks/payments-stripe/index.js (routes, webhook processing, plan checks), stripe.js (the REST client) and signature.js (Stripe-Signature verification) before changing anything. docs.md in the CalmAPI registry has the full setup.
Configuration lives in calm.config.js under blocks['payments-stripe'] (prices, successUrl, cancelUrl, portalReturnUrl, allowedRedirects, activeStatuses, oneSubscription, trialDays, allowPromotionCodes). Keys come from .env: STRIPE_SECRET_KEY and STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET. Never hardcode or log them.
Invariants that must not be broken:
- Never trust a price, amount, plan or customer id from the client. Checkout only sells price ids listed in options.prices; add a price there, never accept arbitrary ones.
- Always verify the Stripe-Signature on ctx.rawBody (the route keeps rawBody: true). Never verify against ctx.body or JSON.stringify(ctx.body), never skip verification in any mode.
- Each event id is processed once (calm_billing_events, unique _id). Keep the claim before the side effects, and delete it on failure so Stripe retries.
- The webhook is the source of truth for plans. Do not grant a plan from the success page or a client call; read billing state with app.ext.billing.plansOf(userId) / hasPlan().
- Redirect URLs (successUrl, cancelUrl, returnUrl) must stay restricted to allowedRedirects (default: the APP_URL origin).
- Events can arrive out of order or twice: keep the lastEventAt guard and never move a canceled subscription back to active.
Common tasks: gate a route with meta: { plan: 'pro' } (402 PLAN_REQUIRED), or a policy: 'plan-pro' named policy, or policy: requirePlan('pro') imported from app/blocks/payments-stripe/index.js. React to billing with calm.on('billing.subscription_updated' | 'billing.subscription_canceled' | 'billing.payment_failed' | 'billing.payment_succeeded' | 'billing.checkout_completed', fn). Handle a new Stripe event type by adding it to HANDLED and to handle() in index.js.
Pitfalls: unknown event types must still answer 200 (or Stripe retries for days); the webhook route must stay policy: 'public' (Stripe has no session) and outside guards that need a user; test keys in production and live keys in development are reported by calm doctor.
Tests: use a fake Stripe server (node:http) and blocks['payments-stripe'].apiBase, sign events with signStripePayload() from signature.js, as test/blocks/payments-stripe.test.js in the CalmAPI repo does. Build test keys at runtime, never commit key-shaped literals.
